lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Northside Bakery | Delivery Driver | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Delivered morning wholesale orders to about 20 cafés and collected signed invoices.
- Loaded the van and checked each order against the dispatch list before leaving.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Jul 2021 - Feb 2023
- Owned the end-of-line test station for the humidity sensor and the yield reports the line leads used.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Built a solar-powered weather station on an STM32 that reports every 5 minutes over LoRa and runs 9 days without sun.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- Wrote the CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard and tested it against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, osciloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Check that the phone number and code URL are your intended public contact details.
Check that the code URL opens directly to work you want an employer to see.
Put Voltline before Clearwater and Northside.
items.because: Work experience should be in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Consider placing the current delivery job below the engineering roles or in Additional Experience.
items.because: It should not lead the technical case for an embedded role.

items.says: Consider moving Education below Experience.
items.because: Your professional results are now stronger evidence than the degree.

items.says: Fix the corrupted character the review identifies in “cafØs.”
Add a result or shorten the loading and checking bullet.
items.because: It describes a duty rather than an outcome.

items.says: Specify what you controlled or improved at the test station.
items.because: “Owned” and “yield reports” establish responsibility but not the effect of your work.

items.says: Clarify the period or population behind the return rates.
items.because: The comparison needs to be credible.

items.says: Clarify whether “15 to 2 a quarter” counts customer complaints in comparable quarters.
Check that the before-and-after throughput was measured on a comparable basis.
Specify what was 60% faster and how it was measured.
Clarify whether the 400 tests ran automatically on every build and what coverage or failures the rig added.
Clarify whether the logger helped diagnose five failures or led to fixes.
items.because: “Found the root cause” may overstate what the logger alone did.

items.says: Correct or remove the claim that sampling an unfiltered 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz avoids aliasing.
items.because: The Nyquist rate would need to exceed 10 kHz unless another technique made the approach valid.

items.says: Correct or remove the claim that declaring the counter volatile fixed a race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not by itself fix a race condition or make access atomic.

items.says: Move the motor-controller rewrite near the top of the Voltline bullets.
items.because: It is an excellent lead bullet.

items.says: Verify that the 300-unit scope and both improvements are attributable to this work.
Clarify the test conditions for “9 days without sun.”
items.because: The figure may depend materially on battery size, weather, or reporting interval.

items.says: Check that the current figures were measured under comparable operating conditions.
Add a direct project link if the designs are public.
Clarify whether you led the full 12-person team or its electronics work.
items.because: “Electronics Lead, Team of 12” can mean either.

items.says: Remove the robot-fleet firmware bullet or replace it with work done on the car.
items.because: It conflicts with the Formula Student project context.

items.says: Specify your contribution or a test result for the dashboard CAN work if you have room.
Remove the 300-robot motor-control bullet.
items.because: It appears to duplicate the Voltline achievement and does not belong under Formula Student.

items.says: Correct the spelling of “osciloscopes.”
Consider separating languages, hardware or platforms, and instruments.
items.because: It could make the list easier to scan.

items.says: Consider naming specific embedded techniques you used instead of the broad term “firmware.”
